limitations: Independent fresh 13-round snake redraft; real keepers, traded picks, trades, and rosters are unchanged.
Baseline: ten active slots, three bench spots, four acquisitions per matchup period, and a one-day dropped-player cooldown.
No injured-reserve slots are used. Shared free agents are processed in rotating deterministic team order, which differs from ESPN waiver priority.
All players lock together at the first NBA game of the day; each daily lineup is selected once.
Percentage categories are tied when either team has zero attempts; otherwise made/attempted totals are compared.
Four-team playoffs use the final two playoff period ranges; tied series advance the higher regular-season seed.
Regular-season seeds use category winning percentage, then matchup wins, then the reproducible draft order.
Forecasts are fixed at draft, then updated only after completed games. Missing rows on a complete game day count as no statistics.
Initial forecast cutoff: 2026-10-07T14:23:48.998Z.
Results use ESPN NBA regular-season box scores, including players outside the real fantasy rosters. Incomplete or mismatched scoring days are not finalized.
NBA game dates use America/New_York; matchup boundaries come from the ESPN basketball calendar, including its extended All-Star period.
ESPN statistics can be corrected after a game. Previously finalized dates require an explicit rebuild to incorporate later corrections.
Player values use current ESPN season projections, falling back to prior-season per-game averages. Players without complete forecasts receive a zero baseline.
Live player eligibility, injuries, forecasts and NBA schedules reflect the latest successful capture. Decisions must be saved before games start to count as prospective.

limitations: Sixteen separate prospective experiments: one franchise is automated in each, while the other seven keep their actual dated lineups. Official ownership and the whole-league AI run are unchanged.

The completed public app draft board, including revealed keeper slots and traded picks, is the draft authority. Nothing is redrafted until all 104 real selections are known. The one-team redraft reserves the seven owners’ real selections as an explicit experiment constraint.
Post-draft teams start from their actual draft roster. AI management begins on the first NBA scoring date. Offseason owner changes to that controlled franchise are not copied into its AI roster.
Ten active positions, thirteen roster spots, no IR, at most one acquisition per day and four per matchup period. Drops and newly observed owner releases have a one-day cooldown.

Daily decisions are saved before the first NBA tipoff using captured owner rosters, current eligibility/injuries, and forecasts learned only from already completed dates. All players lock together. A missed lock stays a gap; no historical decisions are invented.

Other owners’ claims take priority at the next AI decision boundary. Intraday owner moves after that boundary cannot rewrite the saved AI lineup; actual opponents still receive their observed daily scoring.

Owner daily scoring is reconstructed from dated ESPN lineup slots and verified NBA box scores. Completed periods are checked against ESPN category totals; discrepancies block championship certification rather than silently changing player statistics.

Standings use completed regular periods; the top four are reseeded into the final two playoff ranges. Ties use category percentage, matchup wins, then the verified original draft order. A tied playoff series advances the higher seed.

The daily scheduled source refresh runs at 10:15 UTC. It captures the next decision early that morning, not immediately before tipoff; later injuries or lineup announcements cannot change that locked decision.

limitations: Independent fresh 13-round snake redraft; real keepers, traded picks, trades, and rosters are unchanged.
Baseline: ten active slots, three bench spots, four acquisitions per matchup period, and a one-day dropped-player cooldown.
No injured-reserve slots are used. Shared free agents are processed in rotating deterministic team order, which differs from ESPN waiver priority.
All players lock together at the first NBA game of the day; each daily lineup is selected once.
Percentage categories are tied when either team has zero attempts; otherwise made/attempted totals are compared.
Four-team playoffs use the final two playoff period ranges; tied series advance the higher regular-season seed.
Regular-season seeds use category winning percentage, then matchup wins, then the reproducible draft order.
Forecasts are fixed at draft, then updated only after completed games. Missing rows on a complete game day count as no statistics.
Initial forecast cutoff: 2025-07-01T00:00:00.000Z.
Results use ESPN NBA regular-season box scores, including players outside the real fantasy rosters. Incomplete or mismatched scoring days are not finalized.
NBA game dates use America/New_York; matchup boundaries come from the ESPN basketball calendar, including its extended All-Star period.
ESPN statistics can be corrected after a game. Previously finalized dates require an explicit rebuild to incorporate later corrections.

Historical replay is a reconstructed prior-stat baseline, not archived preseason AI intelligence: only 2024–25 actual per-game averages drive player values. No 2025–26 outcomes, present rankings or present injuries enter those values.

The baseline date identifies when the prior NBA season had finished; the data was retrieved later. Historical player eligibility and the available player universe come from the ESPN season endpoint and may include later changes.
Daily historical roster availability is reconstructed from box-score rosters, including DNP players. Historical injury reports, waiver eligibility and announcements at lineup lock are unavailable.
Players without a complete prior-season average receive a zero baseline; rookies and other newcomers are therefore disadvantaged. This is an explicit limitation of the replay.
